newsitem.title: UK: UK plans comprehensive review of public spending.
newsitem.headline: UK plans comprehensive review of public spending.

text.p: British ministers are to undertake a thorough review of all items of public spending, and look at the possible disposal of surplus public assets, Chief Secretary to the Treasury Alistair Darling said on Thursday.
In a parliamentary written answer, Darling said the review would be "truly comprehensive, embracing all items of public expenditure".

"Ministers have agreed that they will examine each and every item in his or her department to consider whether it meets the public interest, whether it contributes to the achievement of the Government's objectives, whether it is the most efficient way of achieving these objectives and whether there is scope for improving efficiency and effectiveness," Darling said.

"This will include a thorough look at whether the best use is being made of public assets, with a view to disposing of those which are surplus and which could be used more productively elsewhere and making more use of public/private partnerships," he added.

Darling announced last month that the government would conduct a "Comprehensive Spending Review" to chart the weay forward after the two years when it has said it will basically following spending plans drawn up by its Conservative predecessor. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
